info.name: United HRMS - Identity + Employees
info.description: Authentication/RBAC (Identity, Phase 5) and Employee CRUD (Employee module, Phase 6) endpoints. Run requests top-to-bottom within each folder. Folder 6 (Employee Management) requires the access_token captured by folder 2's 'Login (Admin)' request, and a department_id — see that folder's first request for how to get one.

request.description: No auth required. Expect 200, status: healthy, database and redis both healthy: true.

Bootstrap: run this first. Requires the admin account already created via `manage.py create_admin_user` (see run instructions). Captures access_token and refresh_token for every other request in this collection.
Same error whether the email is wrong or the password is wrong — this is deliberate, see IDENTITY_API.md.
Rotates the refresh token. Run 'Refresh Token - Replay Old Token' immediately after this to see the old one get rejected.

exec: pm.test("New refresh token differs from old", function () {

request.description: Must run AFTER 'Refresh Token' — proves a rotated-out refresh token cannot be reused.

Must run AFTER 'Logout' using the SAME access_token — proves logout actually revokes the access token, not just the refresh token. NOTE: re-run 'Login (Admin)' afterward before continuing to the next folders, since access_token is now revoked.

exec: pm.test("Status is 401 - access token was revoked at logout", function () {

request.description:
Always returns 200. The reset token is NOT in this response (by design) — find it in the backend container logs: 
docker compose -f infra/docker-compose.yml logs backend | grep 'Password reset'
Paste it into the 'reset_token' collection variable before running the next request.
Requires 'reset_token' collection variable to be set manually from the container logs first.

exec: pm.test("Status is 401 - old password no longer works", function () {

Requires identity.manage_users — run 'Login (Admin)' first so access_token is an admin token.

request.description: Uses new_user_access_token (a plain user with no roles) — proves RBAC is enforced, not just documented. Run 'Login as New User' first.

Requires employees.manage_employees (HR Admin has it by default) — run 'Login (Admin)' in folder 2 first. Requires 'department_id' collection variable to be set first: docker compose -f infra/docker-compose.yml --env-file .env exec backend python manage.py shell -c "from apps.employees.infrastructure.models import DepartmentRecord; [print(d.code, d.id) for d in DepartmentRecord.objects.all()]" — departments GEN/ENG/HR are seeded automatically by migration 0003. Captures employee_id for every other request in this folder.
Must run AFTER 'Create Employee' — same work_email, proves the uniqueness check.
Requires employees.view_employees (HR Admin has it by default). Run 'Create Employee' first.
Accepts ?department_id=, ?employment_status=, ?employment_type=, ?ordering=, ?page=, ?page_size=.
Matches q/search against first name, last name, employee_code, work_email — see EMPLOYEE_API.md.
Full-replace update, bound to PATCH — every field is required (see EMPLOYEE_API.md).
ACTIVE -> SUSPENDED.
SUSPENDED -> ACTIVE. Must run AFTER 'Deactivate Employee'.
Uses new_user_access_token from folder 4 (a plain user with no roles) — proves RBAC is enforced here too. Run 'Login as New User' (folder 4) first.
